senses.definition: Right or suitable for the situation, or following a rule or accepted practice.
senses.example: It is proper to return a borrowed book in good condition.

senses.definition: Writing in ordinary sentences and paragraphs rather than in lines of poetry.
senses.example: The book tells one chapter in verse and the next in prose.

senses.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm or damage.
senses.example: The case protects my glasses when I put them in my bag.

senses.definition: A material built from small parts called amino acids. Different proteins have different jobs in living things.
senses.example: One protein in my blood carries oxygen.

senses.definition: An action or event that shows people strongly disagree with something.
senses.example: The families held a protest asking the town to keep the park open.

senses.definition: To say or show that you strongly disagree with something.
senses.example: I protested when the game ended before our final turn.

senses.definition: To stick out from or beyond a surface.
senses.example: A corner of the blanket protruded from the closed box.

senses.definition: Pleased because you or someone you care about did something well.
senses.example: I was proud of my friend when she finished the steep climb.

senses.definition: A short well-known saying that gives advice or shares a general idea about life.
senses.example: “Many hands make light work” is a proverb about helping each other.

senses.definition: A large area within a country that has a name and its own local government in many places.
senses.example: Ontario is a province in Canada.

senses.definition: To move quietly while watching or looking for something.
senses.example: The cat prowled around the garden after dark.

senses.definition: Work or help provided for people by a government or another group acting for it.
senses.example: Fire protection is a public service our town helps pay for.

senses.definition: To make writing, pictures, or other work available for people to read or see.
senses.example: Our class plans to publish a book of poems.

senses.definition: A small flat disk moved with sticks in ice hockey.
senses.example: The puck slid across the ice to the other player.

senses.definition: A small shallow pool of water or another liquid on a surface.
senses.example: I stepped over a puddle at the corner.

senses.definition: A quick small burst of air, smoke, or steam.
senses.example: A puff of air from the window moved the paper.

senses.definition: To send out air or smoke in small bursts.
senses.example: The old train puffed steam as it started up.

senses.definition: A seabird with a thick, brightly colored bill during the breeding season.
senses.example: A puffin carried small fish back to its nest.

senses.definition: To move something toward you or in the direction you are moving.
senses.example: Pull the wagon toward the shed.

senses.definition: A steady or sudden force that draws something closer.
senses.example: One pull on the curtain cord opened the curtains.

senses.definition: A wheel with a groove along its edge that guides a rope or cable.
senses.example: The rope passed over a pulley so we could pull down to lift the flag.

senses.definition: A wet mixture of little fibers used to make paper.
senses.example: The paper machine squeezed water out of the pulp.

senses.definition: A beat you can feel when pressure from the heart moves through an artery.
senses.example: A heartbeat starts the pressure change you notice as a pulse.

senses.definition: A large wild cat found in the Americas, also called a cougar or mountain lion.
senses.example: A wildlife camera caught a puma walking quietly at night.

senses.definition: A round or ridged squash, often orange, with firm flesh and many seeds.
senses.example: We planted a pumpkin seed at one edge of the garden.

senses.definition: A stiff card whose holes in particular places stand for information.
senses.example: The machine used the holes on each punch card to add to a count.

senses.definition: Arriving or happening at the time that was planned.
senses.example: Lena was punctual and got to the bus stop before we left.

senses.definition: Marks in writing, such as periods and question marks, that help show how the words fit together or should be read.
senses.example: We checked the punctuation before turning in our stories.

senses.definition: A small hole made by something sharp.
senses.example: A puncture in the tire let the air out.

senses.definition: To make a hole by poking or piercing something.
senses.example: A sharp thorn punctured the soft rubber.

senses.definition: A penalty received after breaking a rule or doing something wrong.
senses.example: The referee gave the team a time penalty as punishment for breaking the rule.

senses.definition: The round opening that lets light into an eye.
senses.example: My pupil becomes smaller in bright light.

senses.definition: A figure moved by someone’s hands, strings, or rods, often to act out a story.
senses.example: We made a puppet from a sock and two paper eyes.

senses.definition: To buy something.
senses.example: We purchased two tickets before getting on the ferry.

senses.definition: Something you buy, or the act of buying it.
senses.example: The bird guide was my favorite purchase at the sale.

senses.definition: Made of just one thing with nothing else mixed in.
senses.example: The shop sold pure apple juice with no added sweetener.

senses.definition: The reason for doing something or the job a thing was made to do.
senses.example: The purpose of the covering is to keep rain off the seats.

senses.definition: Done with a clear aim or with determination.
senses.example: She took purposeful steps toward the stage even though she was nervous.

senses.definition: A small bag used to carry money or personal things.
senses.example: I found the bus pass inside my purse.

senses.definition: To draw the lips together into a small rounded shape.
senses.example: He pursed his lips as he tried to whistle.

senses.definition: To use force to move something away from you or in a certain direction.
senses.example: We pushed the cart toward the old gate.

senses.definition: A movement or force that presses something in a direction.
senses.example: One strong push sent the empty sled down the hill.

senses.definition: To move or place someone or something somewhere.
senses.example: I put the dirty cup beside the sink.

senses.definition: To express an idea in a certain way.
senses.example: “Let’s give it another try” is a kind way to put it.

senses.definition: To return something to a storage place after using it.
senses.example: We put away the paintbrushes after washing them.

senses.definition: To move something you planned to do to a later time.
senses.example: Rain forced us to put off the picnic for a day.

senses.definition: To notice how separate clues fit and use them to work out what probably happened.
senses.example: When I saw muddy boots and tracks by the door, I put two and two together.

senses.definition: A problem, picture, or game meant to be worked out by thinking.
senses.example: We finished the puzzle and saw a picture of a sailboat.

senses.definition: To make someone think hard because something is confusing or unexpected.
senses.example: The footprints in the dry sand puzzled me.
